A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVG-EAR work. Their complete main text and appendices are readable, including visually verified equations, figures, tables, and algorithms; material can be matched across layout and numbering changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-generation benchmarks, attention-error analyses, kernel timing measurements, and qualitative comparisons in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds stability measurements, a video-quality ablation, and clustering sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same clustering, centroid compensation, value-aware error estimation, error-to-cost routing, and kernel algorithms. The added ablations test existing components rather than introduce a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Penguin Benchmark text prompts and VBench image-prompt pairs for the same Wan2.2 and HunyuanVideo generation tasks. The added analyses remain within existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix F adds SVG2 with compensation but unchanged block selection to the Wan2.2 T2V PSNR comparison. V1 evaluated this variant only through attention-map MSE in Figure 6. Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces a clustering sweep over query/key counts of (300,1000), (100,1000), (300,500), (100,500), and (50,500), explicitly retaining other main-experiment settings. Existing sample counts, resolutions, benchmark metrics, warmups, and Table 3 configurations are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends the retained attention-level analyses with a video-level compensation/routing ablation in Appendix F and clustering sensitivity and overhead measurements in Appendix G. Sections 5.1 and 5.3 also add normalizer and reconstruction-error stability findings. These are focused extensions of existing analyses.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports reconstruction-error variation within 4.75% at 300 query clusters, but does not define what varies or how this statistic was obtained. Whether it represents statistical uncertainty or a deterministic stability measure is unclear. Neither version specifies seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark tables and plots retain their results. Additions include 24.157 PSNR for SVG2 with compensation, 4.18% average relative normalizer change, the 4.75% variation statement, and Table 5 results spanning PSNR 22.501–24.995 and speedups 1.59–1.75×. These are additional measurements, not improvements to previously reported benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, estimators, normalizer-stability assumption, error bound, and Appendix A proof are unchanged. Propositions 1 and 2 become 4.1 and A.1. The new empirical assumption check does not revise the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free compensation and error-aware routing contributions, theoretical guarantee, Pareto-frontier claim, and headline quality and speedup claims.

C2.justification: V2 newly interprets the 4.75% reconstruction-error variation as stability at 300 query clusters. Appendix G interprets the clustering sweep as having little effect on quality with small overhead. The stated limitation concerning applicability beyond DiTs is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G and Table 5 document the exact clustering configurations for the added sensitivity study and state that other settings follow the main experiments. Existing kernel pseudocode, baseline hyperparameters, hardware information, and dataset-selection descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Re-ttention, MInference 1.0, and DiTFastAttnV2 to the static sparse-attention discussion. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. V2 adds keywords, acknowledgements, and short Appendices F and G; the existing visualization appendix becomes H. Citation style, proposition numbering, and some table terminology also change.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the entire document with narrower text blocks, different typography, running headers, resized and relocated figures, and reformatted tables. Figure 1 moves off the title page. Table 5 is added, while the existing Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–4 remain.

improvement.justification: The added video-quality ablation, clustering sensitivity table, and normalizer check provide useful support beyond v1's existing analyses. The gains are limited: experimental descriptions remain terse, and Appendix G's claim of little quality sensitivity is optimistic given Table 5's PSNR range of 22.501–24.995. The main benchmark results and theory remain unchanged.
